beginner_glossary.Bitcoin mining (legacy business): Running specialized computers to validate Bitcoin transactions and earn Bitcoin rewards. This was IREN's original business (97% of FY2025 revenue) and is now being WOUND DOWN as the company shifts that power and those data centers to AI.
beginner_glossary.AI cloud / neocloud: Renting out AI computing (NVIDIA GPUs) at scale to companies that need it. IREN is converting from a Bitcoin miner into an 'AI cloud' provider — a neocloud, like CoreWeave or Nebius.
beginner_glossary.Secured power (gigawatts, GW): Electricity capacity IREN has locked up via grid contracts — the scarcest input in AI infrastructure. IREN has 5 GW SECURED (not just a pipeline), one of the largest such portfolios in the world. 1 GW ≈ a large power plant.
beginner_glossary.Time to compute: IREN's key metric — how fast it can turn secured power into customer-ready, revenue-generating GPU compute. Because demand far exceeds supply, whoever delivers compute soonest wins.
beginner_glossary.ARR (Annual Recurring Revenue) under con: The yearly revenue value of contracts already SIGNED. IREN has $3.1B of ARR under contract and targets $3.7B exiting calendar 2026 — the clearest bridge from capacity to revenue.
beginner_glossary.Liquid-cooled vs air-cooled: Two ways to cool GPUs. LIQUID-cooled handles the densest, newest chips (e.g., the Microsoft 'Horizon' build) but costs more and takes longer to build. AIR-cooled is cheaper and FASTER (great for retrofitting existing mining sites), giving IREN a speed advantage to capture demand quickly.
beginner_glossary.Retrofit / conversion: Taking IREN's EXISTING (air-cooled) Bitcoin-mining data centers and converting them to run AI GPUs — capital-efficient and fast because the power, land, and buildings already exist.
beginner_glossary.GPU (Blackwell / Rubin / H100): NVIDIA's AI chips. 'Blackwell' is the current generation IREN is deploying; 'Rubin' is NVIDIA's next platform (Sweetwater One is designed for it); H100/A100 are older but still fully utilized.
beginner_glossary.NVIDIA DSX / DGX / AI Factory: NVIDIA reference designs for building AI data centers. IREN is deploying 'DSX-aligned' infrastructure — i.e., building to NVIDIA's blueprint, deepening the partnership.
beginner_glossary.Managed services deployment: IREN doesn't just rent bare GPUs; for the NVIDIA contract it also manages/operates the AI infrastructure for the customer — a higher-value service (helped by the Mirantis acquisition).
beginner_glossary.Vertical integration: Owning and controlling the whole critical path — power, land, data-center construction, and GPU deployment. IREN argues this lets it deliver faster and more reliably than rivals who depend on third parties.
beginner_glossary.Prepayments & GPU financing: How IREN funds expensive GPUs: customers PAY UPFRONT (prepayments) and IREN borrows against the GPUs/contracts (GPU financing). It funded ~95% of the Microsoft GPU capex this way at ~3% interest.
beginner_glossary.Adjusted EBITDA: A proxy for cash operating profit (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, amortization, and some one-offs). IREN's was $59.5M in Q3 FY2026 — positive, unlike its GAAP net loss.
beginner_glossary.Non-cash impairment: An accounting write-down (no cash leaves the company) — here, mostly from RETIRING old mining hardware as IREN pivots to AI. These drove most of the quarter's reported net loss.
beginner_glossary.EH/s (exahashes per second): A measure of Bitcoin-mining computing power. IREN reached 50 EH/s — but this legacy capacity is now being repurposed toward AI.
beginner_glossary.P/E vs EV/ARR: P/E (price ÷ earnings) is unreliable here because earnings are distorted by impairments and Bitcoin swings. Investors instead value IREN on its CONTRACTED ARR and secured-power build-out.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: IREN is an Australia-founded, U.S.-listed data-center company transforming from a Bitcoin MINER into an AI-cloud / AI-infrastructure provider. In the AI/semiconductor supply chain it is a NEOCLOUD / data-center node: it secures power and land, builds (and retrofits) data centers, deploys NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI compute — now anchored by major contracts with Microsoft and NVIDIA. Its edge is VERTICAL INTEGRATION (it controls power, land, and construction) and a huge 5 GW secured-power portfolio. It is both a large NVIDIA CUSTOMER and an NVIDIA INVESTEE (up to $2.1B investment tied to GPU deployment).
company_snapshot.headquarters: Sydney, Australia (data centers across the U.S. — Texas, British Columbia/Canada — and expanding into Europe/Spain and APAC/Australia)
company_snapshot.founder_ceo: Co-founders & Co-CEOs: Daniel Roberts and Will Roberts (brothers). Key execs: Anthony Lewis (capital/CFO function), Kent Draper (Chief Commercial Officer).
company_snapshot.manufacturing_footprint: Owns/controls a global power-and-data-center platform: 5 GW SECURED power. U.S. campuses: Childress & Sweetwater (Texas), plus Kiowa (Oklahoma) and British Columbia (Canada — Prince George, Mackenzie, Canal Flats). Europe via the Nostrum acquisition (Spain, 490 MW secured + GW-scale pipeline). APAC pipeline anchored in Australia. ~3,000 workers on-site at Childress alone. [Q3 FY2026 call 2026-05-07]

business_model.summary: IREN makes money two ways today, but the mix is flipping. The LEGACY business is Bitcoin mining (earning Bitcoin from computing power) — still the majority of revenue but shrinking as IREN decommissions mining gear. The FUTURE business is AI cloud: securing power and land, building/retrofitting data centers, deploying NVIDIA GPUs, and renting AI compute (increasingly with managed services). The strategy is to convert its scarce 5 GW of secured power into customer-ready compute faster than rivals ('time to compute'), pre-contract that capacity (with anchors like Microsoft and NVIDIA), and use those contracts plus customer prepayments to raise cheap financing for the build-out.
how_they_make_money: AI cloud services (the future): renting NVIDIA GPU compute + managed services to hyperscalers, AI labs, and enterprises; $33.6M revenue in Q3 FY2026 (up from $17.3M QoQ) and ramping toward $3.7B ARR. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Bitcoin mining (the legacy, declining): $111.2M revenue in Q3 FY2026 (down from $167.4M) as hardware is decommissioned and redirected to AI. [Q3 FY2026 call]

Contracted-but-not-yet-recognized ARR: $3.1B under contract (Microsoft 'Horizon' liquid-cooled builds + the $3.54B NVIDIA AI-cloud contract) that converts to revenue as capacity comes online. [Q3 FY2026 call]
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Secured power at scale: 5 GW SECURED (not pipeline) — power is the binding constraint on AI infrastructure, and IREN has one of the largest portfolios anywhere. [Q3 FY2026 call]

Vertical integration + repeatable construction: controls power, land, and data-center build with standardized, parallel construction templates (Childress as the proven model) — 'time to compute' advantage. [Q3 FY2026 call]

NVIDIA partnership: up to $2.1B NVIDIA investment (vesting as GPUs deploy, fully at 600k GPUs), DSX-aligned builds, early Rubin access, and NVIDIA referrals — a powerful demand and validation anchor. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Speed via air-cooled retrofits: converting existing mining sites to AI quickly and cheaply — a commercial edge when the shortest-timeline capacity is the most valuable. [Q3 FY2026 call]
Mirantis acquisition: 650 engineers + cloud/Kubernetes/managed-services capability to support enterprise/AI customers beyond bare-metal GPUs. [Q3 FY2026 call]
ASSUMPTION-flavored: real assets and execution capability are genuine moats, but the model is capital-intensive and the AI-cloud business is still early relative to the contracted ambition.

revenue_streams.analyst_view: IREN's income statement is a snapshot of a company mid-pivot: ~77% of revenue is still the SHRINKING Bitcoin-mining business, while the ~23% AI-cloud slice is small but nearly doubling sequentially and carries essentially all the strategic value ($3.1B contracted ARR vs. ~$134M annualized AI revenue today). That gap — between tiny reported AI revenue and huge contracted ARR — is the whole story: the bet is that the secured power and signed contracts convert into a multi-billion AI-cloud business over 2026–2028. Until then, reported revenue/earnings will look weak and noisy (mining decline + impairments), which is why the stock trades on ARR and power, not the current P&L.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: IREN's edge versus other neoclouds and miners-turned-AI is the breadth of SECURED POWER (5 GW), genuine vertical integration (power + land + construction in-house), and the speed/capital-efficiency of converting existing air-cooled mining sites to AI. financial_performance.analyst_view: IREN's financials must be read as a company in transition. FY2025 net income of $86.9M and TTM net income of ~$158M look fine but are mining-era and Bitcoin-price-driven; the latest quarter swung to a $247.8M LOSS almost entirely on non-cash impairments from RETIRING mining gear — a sign the pivot is real, not a deterioration of the AI business (which is growing and adjusted-EBITDA positive at $59.5M). The signal to watch is the gap between ~$134M annualized AI revenue today and $3.1B contracted ARR: if IREN converts secured power to compute on schedule and funds it (largely via prepayments + ~3% GPU financing), the AI-cloud business inflects dramatically; if not, the stock's premium unwinds.

valuation.analyst_view: IREN is a high-beta bet on a Bitcoin miner successfully becoming an AI-infrastructure company. The bull case: 5 GW of scarce secured power, $3.1B contracted ARR with Microsoft + NVIDIA anchors, vertical-integration speed, cheap contract-backed financing, and NVIDIA as investor/partner/customer. The bear case: it must execute a massive, capital-hungry build-out, still carries Bitcoin-price noise and impairments, faces customer/NVIDIA concentration and a crowded field of miners-turned-AI, and trades at a premium on FUTURE ARR with a $41 analyst floor implying ~30% downside. The debate is execution + financing risk versus a genuinely scarce power/contract position — not whether AI demand exists.

risks.why_it_matters: Building 5 GW needs multi-year, multi-billion capital; if prepayments/GPU financing/capital markets tighten, the build (and ARR ramp) stalls — the central risk.
Revenue depends on delivering power, data centers, and GPU commissioning on tight, back-end-weighted timelines; delays push out ARR conversion.
Microsoft and NVIDIA anchor the contracted ARR and IREN's strategy/cap table; over-reliance on a few counterparties is a risk if one changes course.
Remaining mining revenue and balance-sheet Bitcoin tie results to a volatile BTC price; mining decommissioning also drives recurring non-cash impairments.
The thesis assumes demand keeps outstripping supply; an AI-capex digestion or a surge of GPU supply would hit utilization, pricing, and contracting.
Priced on FUTURE ARR (~6–7x contracted) with a 52-week range of $9.52–$76.87 and a $41 analyst floor; any stumble can cause large drawdowns.
Equity raises and convertible notes (and cap-call dynamics) can dilute shareholders, especially if the stock falls or financing needs rise.
CoreWeave, Nebius, Core Scientific/Applied Digital/TeraWulf, and the hyperscalers all compete for power, GPUs, customers, and capital.
Grid connection, permitting, and community/political pushback can slow or block capacity additions across regions.
Reported losses/impairments during the mining-to-AI shift can spook investors and obscure the underlying AI-business trajectory.

scenarios.disclaimer: Illustrative scenarios to frame the range of outcomes — NOT predictions, targets, or advice.

bull_case.thesis: IREN executes the pivot: it converts its 5 GW secured power into contracted compute on schedule, ARR scales from $3.1B toward and beyond $3.7B, the NVIDIA and Microsoft relationships compound, and cheap contract-backed financing funds the build — turning a Bitcoin miner into a major, profitable AI-infrastructure platform.
key_drivers: 480 MW (2026) → 1.21 GW (2027) delivered on time; capacity contracted before/at commissioning; no idle GPUs.
NVIDIA investment vests as GPUs deploy; new hyperscaler/AI-native/enterprise contracts diversify the book.
Air-cooled retrofits + liquid-cooled builds ramp; adjusted EBITDA and (eventually) clean profitability inflect up.
Europe (Spain) and APAC (Australia) add growth; the stock re-rates toward/above the ~$82 median target.
bull_case.what_to_watch: ARR vs the $3.7B target; capacity-online milestones; financing terms; new contract wins; AI-cloud revenue inflection.

base_case.thesis: A real but lumpy transformation: IREN delivers most of its 2026 capacity, ARR ramps meaningfully (back-end-weighted), mining keeps shrinking with periodic impairments, and IREN becomes a credible mid-tier AI-infrastructure player — with the stock volatile around execution and financing headlines.
key_drivers: AI-cloud revenue ramps as Microsoft + the new GPUs come online; ARR climbs toward the target with some slippage.
Financing stays available (prepayments + ~3% GPU financing + asset-level debt) with manageable dilution.
5 GW build progresses on an S-curve; Sweetwater/Kiowa/Spain advance.
Stock tracks ARR/secured-power multiples, swinging with AI sentiment and BTC.
base_case.what_to_watch: Quarterly AI-cloud revenue + adjusted EBITDA; ARR progression; financing announcements; mining wind-down pace.

bear_case.thesis: The capital-heavy build outruns affordable financing or AI demand digests; capacity/ARR slips, impairments and dilution mount, Bitcoin weakness adds drag, and a stock priced on future ARR de-rates sharply (analyst floor ~$41 implies ~30% downside).
key_drivers: Financing tightens or terms worsen; capex outpaces funding; build slows.
Construction/commissioning delays or an AI-demand pause leave capacity uncontracted or idle.
Customer/NVIDIA concentration bites; competition pressures pricing; BTC falls.
Heavy dilution; the ~6–7x contracted-ARR multiple compresses.
bear_case.what_to_watch: Financing strain or dilutive raises; capacity/ARR misses; AI-capex commentary; BTC price; impairment trend.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: IREN Limited (IREN) is an Australia-founded, NASDAQ-listed company transforming from a Bitcoin MINER into an AI-cloud / data-center provider — in the AI supply chain it is a neocloud that secures power and land, builds (and retrofits) data centers, deploys NVIDIA GPUs, and rents AI compute. Its reported numbers are mid-transition and noisy: FY2025 (ended June 2025) revenue was $501M with $86.9M net income, but ~97% was Bitcoin mining; in Q3 FY2026 (reported 2026-05-07) revenue was $144.8M (mining $111.2M shrinking, AI cloud $33.6M nearly doubling QoQ) and the company posted a $247.8M net LOSS — almost entirely non-cash impairments from RETIRING mining gear — while still generating $59.5M adjusted EBITDA and ending April with $2.6B cash. The real story is the pivot's scale: IREN has 5 GW of SECURED power (one of the largest portfolios anywhere), $3.1B of ARR UNDER CONTRACT (targeting $3.7B exiting 2026), a 300 MW liquid-cooled Microsoft 'Horizon' build, and a landmark NVIDIA deal — a $3.54B 5-year AI-cloud contract plus up to $2.1B of NVIDIA investment that vests as GPUs deploy (fully at 600,000 GPUs). Because earnings are distorted by impairments and Bitcoin swings, the ~110x trailing P/E is meaningless; the stock ($59.77, ~$21.4B market cap, 52-week range $9.52–$76.87) is valued on contracted ARR (~6.9x the $3.1B, ~5.8x the $3.7B target) and secured power. What is FACT is a scarce, contracted power-and-AI position with NVIDIA/Microsoft anchors and a vertical-integration edge; what is being PRICED is flawless, on-schedule execution of a multi-billion 5 GW build funded by prepayments + cheap GPU financing. The real debate is execution + financing risk (and a wide $41–$126 analyst spread), not whether AI-infrastructure demand exists.
what_is_fact: FY2025 (ended 2025-06-30): revenue $501M (+168%) — mining $484.6M + AI cloud $16.4M; net income $86.9M; adjusted EBITDA $269.7M. [2025-08-28]
Q3 FY2026: revenue $144.8M (mining $111.2M, AI cloud $33.6M); net LOSS $247.8M (incl. $140.4M non-cash mining-decommissioning impairments); adjusted EBITDA $59.5M; cash $2.6B (Apr 30). [2026-05-07]
Secured power 5 GW; ARR under contract $3.1B; target $3.7B exiting CY2026 across 150k GPUs / 480 MW; 2027 plan scales to 1.21 GW. [2026-05-07]
NVIDIA: $3.54B 5-yr AI-cloud contract (~$700M ARR, 60 MW air-cooled Blackwell at Childress) + up to $2.1B investment vesting on GPU deployment (fully at 600k GPUs). [2026-05-07]

Microsoft: 300 MW liquid-cooled 'Horizon One–Four' at Childress; ~95% of GPU capex funded via prepayments + GPU financing at ~3%. Acquisitions: Nostrum (Spain, 490 MW) + Mirantis (650 engineers). [2026-05-07]
Market (2026-06-12): price $59.77, market cap ~$21.36B, ~357.38M shares, 52-week range $9.52–$76.87, no dividend; trailing P/E ~110x but NOT meaningful. [stockanalysis.com]
what_is_assumption_or_opinion: ASSUMPTION: IREN converts 5 GW of secured power into contracted, revenue-generating compute on schedule (480 MW 2026 → 1.21 GW 2027 → more).
ASSUMPTION: IREN funds the multi-billion build via prepayments + GPU/asset financing + NVIDIA investment + capital markets without excessive dilution.
OPINION: P/E is meaningless here (mining impairments + BTC swings); the stock should be valued on contracted ARR / secured power, and the dominant variables are execution and financing, not demand.
what_to_watch_next: AI-cloud revenue + ARR progression vs the $3.7B 2026 exit target (and the gap to today's ~$134M annualized AI revenue).
FINANCING — GPU/asset financing terms, prepayments, NVIDIA investment vesting, any equity raises and resulting dilution.
Capacity-online milestones (Childress Horizon handoffs to Microsoft; Sweetwater One; air-cooled retrofits) and the back-end-weighted ramp.
New contract wins and customer diversification (hyperscalers, AI-natives, enterprises) beyond Microsoft/NVIDIA.
Mining wind-down pace and impairment trend; Bitcoin-price impact on remaining mining revenue.
Europe (Spain/Nostrum) and APAC (Australia) build progress; competition from CoreWeave/Nebius and other miners-turned-AI.
final_research_summary.no_recommendation_reminder: This report deliberately gives NO buy/sell/hold call. It lays out facts, assumptions, drivers, risks, and scenarios so the reader can form their own view.
